content: Please consult a healthcare professional for comprehensive information about this product and to address your specific health needs. Uses: This medication is primarily used prior to eye examinations, such as refraction tests, and for the treatment of certain eye conditions, including uveitis. It belongs to a class of drugs known as anticholinergics. Application Instructions: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly before applying the eye ointment. 2. To prevent contamination, avoid touching the tip of the tube to your eye, skin, or any other surface. 3. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. 4. Squeeze a strip of ointment (approximately 0.5 cm) into the pouch. 5. Close your eye gently and roll your eyeball in all directions to evenly distribute the medication. 6. If you are using other eye medications (e.g., drops or ointments), wait at least 5–10 minutes before applying the next medication. Regular Use: For optimal benefit, use this medication consistently and avoid missing doses. To help you remember, apply it at the same time(s) each day. Side Effects: Common side effects may include burning, stinging, redness of the eye, eye irritation, or temporary blurred vision. These effects are usually mild and temporary. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this product are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. If you experience any unusual or severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Precautions: Before using atropine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to belladonna alkaloids (e.g., hyoscyamine, scopolamine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. After application, your vision may become temporarily blurred, and your eyes may be more sensitive to light. Protect your eyes in bright light conditions. Infants and small children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication. Ensure the medication does not enter a child’s mouth. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Missed Dose: If you are using this medication on a regular schedule and miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
